In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PLP/PMP- ratio of crude liver homogenates is a more sensitive parameter than the PLP/PMD- ratio for vitamin B6 intake studies.
the PLP content in the crude liver homgenate is more closely correlated with the vitamin B6 intake level than the PLP content of the 100 00 0 g supernatant.
vitamin B6 intake is not the only factor that determines the PLP content of the liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PLP content in liver is a more sensitive index for vitamin B6 deficiency than the PLP/PMP ratio.

the PLP/PMP ratio in liver is not a good index for the vitamin B6 status of rats fed diets with varying vitamin B6 contents, but that the total PMP and PLP contents in liver are good indices for the vitamin B 6 status of these animals.
the PLP content of the liver is not a reliable indicator for vitamin B6 status in the rat.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver PLP content is not an adequate measure for the vitamin B6 nutritional status of rats.
the PLP/PMP ratio in the liver is dependent on the vitamin B6 intake level.
the PLP/PMP ratio is a more sensitive indicator of vitamin B6 status than the total vitamin B6 content in liver.
